title: Local first, global second: section passes then a reconciliation pass
situation: Production evaluation shows accuracy drops on 60-page packets with predictable sections such as intake forms, narrative notes, invoices, and attachments. The current single-pass extraction often captures fields within individual sections but produces duplicate entities, inconsistent totals, and occasional schema-valid output with incorrect relationships.
exam_question: Which task decomposition strategy should this team use first?
correct_option_text: Run section-level extraction passes, then run a reconciliation pass that validates schema, deduplicates entities, and checks cross-section consistency.
why: Predictable packets suit a fixed sequential pipeline: extract locally from each known section so the model sees a small evidence set, then reconcile globally (dedupe by invoice_id, compare totals, check relationships). Adaptive decomposition is for exploration where the next step depends on findings; a single expanded prompt or a summary-first pass hides errors behind valid-looking JSON.
task: Build a four-section packet from the fixtures (the same invoice appears in the Invoices section and again in Attachments). Run one single-pass extraction over the whole packet, then one extraction per section followed by a code-level reconciliation pass. Compare records found, duplicates removed and conflicts flagged.
prompt_template:
<document>
[section: {{section_name}}]
{{section_text}}
</document>
Record the financial document in this section with the extract_invoice tool.
expected_outcome: evidence/cases/UC-31.json shows the single pass returning one record for a packet that holds three distinct documents, and the section pipeline returning four section records reconciled to three unique invoice_ids with the duplicate merged and any total mismatch listed.
rubric: Learner states which checks only make sense in the global pass (dedupe, cross-section totals) and why.
Learner explains why the section pass reduces attention dilution.
Learner can say when adaptive decomposition would be the better choice instead.
